translation.canonical_title: Defamation is collateral damage of radical feminism
translation.displayed_title: Defamation is collateral damage of radical feminism
translation.summary: As with any form of denunciation, its close cousin, defamation, is never far away. The recent appeal trial for defamation brought by Éric Brion bears witness to this. In the dock was Sandra Muller, who originated #balancetonporc. Deemed reckless and outside the scope of sexual harassment, the defendant faced damages (€15 000 at first instance) for her tweet: “#balancetonporc! You too, tell your story, giving the name and details of sexual harassmnt (sic) that you experienced at work. I’m waiting for you.” After a few more minutes, she posted a second message: “You have big breasts. You are my type of woman. I’m going to make you come all night. Eric Brion, former head of Equidia #balancetonporc.” An excess? Many theorists see Twitter in particular as a platform conducive to defamation and mythomania.

citations.translated_citation: My life was shattered after those tweets were published. It was an explosion in my life. [...] I lost the few assignments I had with a consulting firm, I lost my partner, I lost my reputation, and I fell into a deep depression.
